repomix.files: This section contains the contents of the repository's files. 1: # UI Audit 2: 3: This document is the source-level contract for the current game chrome. Gameplay 4: art remains asset-backed; navigation, pause, dashboard, audio, and ad controls 5: are rendered as DOM buttons with lucide-react. 6: 7: ## Color Tokens 8: 9: | Token | Value | Use | 10: | --- | --- | --- | 11: | --game-surface | #fff8e7 | Primary card and modal surface | 12: | --game-surface-soft | #fff0c4 | Warm panel gradient | 13: | --game-surface-deep | #f7ce78 | Panel gradient depth | 14: | --game-ink | #382047 | Main text | 15: | --game-ink-muted | #815a2c | Secondary text and timer label | 16: | --game-accent | #7227b8 | Purple action chrome | 17: | --game-gold | #f6b51b | Gold borders and action emphasis | 18: | --game-orange | #f4771a | Score and primary action emphasis | 19: | --game-brown | #6d3c16 | Headings and icon strokes | 20: | --game-danger | #c83b4d | Lose and danger states | 21: 22: The tokens are declared in src/styles/hyper-ui.css and are consumed by the 23: dashboard and mobile timer. Existing --hyper-* tokens remain as compatibility 24: aliases for the Pixi/Hyper UI layer. 25: 26: ## Controls 27: 28: | Control | Component | Icon source | Behavior | 29: | --- | --- | --- | --- | 30: | Dashboard | Game.tsx | Hyper trophy/cup asset | Opens DashboardScreen and pauses gameplay | 31: | Pause | Game.tsx and PauseOverlay.tsx | Pause, Play | Opens/resumes the pause overlay without resetting the game | 32: | Sound | PauseOverlay.tsx | Volume2, VolumeX | Toggles SFX only | 33: | Music | PauseOverlay.tsx | Music | Toggles music only | 34: | Rewarded ad | RewardAdButton.tsx | Clapperboard | Requests a reward; shared by support, revive, and win flows | 35: | Gameplay support | Game.tsx | Existing Hyper art | Hint, shuffle, and bomb remain game-art controls | 36: 37: Restart is intentionally absent from Pause and Dashboard. It is only exposed 38: from the lose/end-game flow so opening a screen cannot silently reset gameplay. 39: 40: ## Mobile Layout 41: 42: At max-width 1023px, the order is: 43: 44: 1. Top row with timer, cup Dashboard, and Pause controls. 45: 2. Score and lives status row. 46: 3. Gameplay board and its end-state overlays. 47: 4. Hint, shuffle, and bomb support rail. 48: 49: The end-state overlays are children of the board stage, so timeout, lose, revive, 50: and win states cover the gameplay region rather than escaping the mobile frame. 1: # Wink starter kit 2: 3: Everything in this directory is copied **into a game repository**. It is 4: self-contained: nothing here needs a Wink checkout at build time. 5: 6: The normal way to install it is the scaffolder, run once from the Wink 7: repository: 8: 9: ```bash 10: node game-template/init-game.mjs \ 11: --repo /path/to/my-game \ 12: --id <GAME_UUID> \ 13: --slug <game-slug> \ 14: --title "Game title" 15: ``` 16: 17: That copies these files, substitutes the game identity, generates 18: `public/wink-runtime-config.json`, writes `public/wink-bridge.lock.json`, and 19: merges the npm scripts from `package.scripts.json`. 20: 21: ## What lands in the game repository 22: 23: | Path | Purpose | 24: | --- | --- | 25: | `public/wink-bridge.js` | Certified bridge artifact, byte-for-byte | 26: | `public/wink-bridge.lock.json` | Version/protocol/bytes/checksum lock | 27: | `public/wink-runtime-config.json` | Generated public config (5 fields) | 28: | `scripts/wink-contract.mjs` | Single source of truth for every pin | 29: | `scripts/generate-wink-runtime-config.mjs` | Strict public config generator | 30: | `scripts/sync-wink-bridge.mjs` | (Re)writes the bridge lock | 31: | `scripts/verify-wink-bridge.mjs` | Fail-closed bridge + config + entry check | 32: | `scripts/verify-game-config.mjs` | Cross-checks `game.config.sh` against the contract | 33: | `scripts/verify-docker-headers.mjs` | Runs real Nginx and asserts headers | 34: | `src/integrations/wink/wink-bridge.ts` | TypeScript facade for the SDK | 35: | `src/integrations/wink/client.ts` | The game's only Wink adapter | 36: | `src/integrations/wink/__tests__/client.test.ts` | Adapter contract tests | 37: | `etc/default.conf.template` | Nginx with exact `frame-ancestors` | 38: | `Dockerfile` | Multi-stage build from source → Nginx | 39: | `.dockerignore` | Keeps source, secrets, and evidence out of the image | 40: | `game.config.sh` | The only per-game deployment inputs | 41: | `deploy.sh` | Gated check / build-push / deploy / rollback | 42: | `wink-integration.json` | Handoff manifest for `verify-handoff.mjs` | 43: | `artifacts/minigame-pilot/` | Local, git-ignored deploy metadata | 44: 45: ## After scaffolding 46: 47: 1. Load the bridge before game code in the HTML entry: 48: 49: ```html 50: <script src="/wink-bridge.js"></script> 51: <script type="module" src="/src/main.tsx"></script> 52: ``` 53: 54: `verify-wink-bridge.mjs` only requires that no other `src=` or 55: `type="module"` script precedes it, so any bundler layout works. 56: 57: 2. Wire the game into `src/integrations/wink/client.ts` at the five semantic 58: boundaries, then replace every `"TODO"` in `wink-integration.json` with a 59: real description. The verifier rejects `"TODO"` (under 16 characters), so 60: `WINK_HANDOFF_OK` is unreachable until the semantics are documented. 61: 62: 3. Run the gates: 63: 64: ```bash 65: npm run verify:wink-bridge 66: npm test 67: npm run typecheck 68: npm run build 69: ``` 70: 71: 4. Follow `game-template/docs/GAME_DEV_HANDOFF.md` for harness testing and the 72: 13-row behavioural matrix. 73: 74: ## Editing rules 75: 76: - `public/wink-bridge.js` is certified — never hand-edit or re-minify it. 77: - `public/wink-runtime-config.json` is generated — never hand-edit it. 78: - `game.config.sh` has one editable block at the top; everything below it is 79: derived and re-validated by `verify-game-config.mjs`. 80: - `scripts/wink-contract.mjs` is identical in every game. Changing it here 81: desynchronises this game from the platform. 1: # Rendered by the official Nginx image with envsubst at container startup. 2: # ALLOWED_PARENT_ORIGINS is supplied by the deployment
